| Scene description | • Observation block S02-A is beside paths and planting in East Lake Tingtao Scenic Area. Across five bin locations, perception records two overflowing bins, four non-overflowing bins, and one accumulation.<br>• S02-A-01: a gray single bin with a black liner stands beside a paved path, plants, and an information board.<br>• S02-A-02: a black mesh dual-compartment bin stands at the path edge by trees and leaves.<br>• S02-A-03: the same bin type stands before lakeside planting, water, and red-green shrubs.<br>• S02-A-04: a dual-compartment bin marked collection in progress has a tied black bag accumulated on the adjacent path.<br>• S02-A-05: an other-waste bin has a full liner reaching the opening beside planting, trees, and grass. |
| Regulatory basis | • **Responsibility and duties:** park managers should provide and maintain containers and ensure proper sorting, collection, transport, and treatment. Provision, maintenance, inspections, and prompt removal are required under Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 44 ([D-06-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)), and Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 4.5.4 ([D-16-C009](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• **Prohibitions:** organizations and individuals must not casually dump, stockpile, discard, or scatter waste (Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv); Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China, Article 506, [D-01-C002](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• **Technical and sanitation standards:** disposal points should be clean without retained waste or wastewater; containers should be orderly, clean, clearly labeled, inspected to prevent overflow, washed and disinfected, and repaired or replaced when damaged (the Wuhan Guidelines, Section 4.5.4, [D-16-C009](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• **Procedures:** daily removal and progressive separation of disposal, collection, and transport are required (Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 29, [D-06-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• **Liability and penalty conditions:** failing to maintain functional containers requires correction, with CNY 1,000–3,000 for continued non-compliance (Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18(1), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)); improper storage or transfer incurs CNY 5,000–50,000 for organizations under item (2); failure to sort requires correction, with CNY 50,000–500,000 for organizations or CNY 100–1,000 for individuals refusing correction under item (3).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering, or stockpiling incurs CNY 5,000–50,000 for organizations or up to CNY 200 for individuals (Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Substandard container provision requires correction; continued non-compliance incurs CNY 50–500 (Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 44, [D-06-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Substandard containers or toilets may incur CNY 2,000–10,000, or CNY 10,000–20,000 in serious cases (Wuhan Municipal Measures for Relatively Centralized Administrative Penalty Powers in Urban Management, Article 12, [D-10-C008](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two overflows and one accumulation breach basic no-overflow and no-retained-waste requirements, although pollution and sanitation impacts are not extensive. Waste beside the path affects visitors and sanitation and suggests management omissions. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: the exposed tied bag beside the path at S02-A-04 causes visual pollution and risks odors and vectors; spillage at S02-A-05 impairs path cleanliness. Possible short-term impacts: delayed removal may encourage visitor littering and pollute planting; cloudy, humid conditions may accelerate organic decay, odors, and vector breeding. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** incomplete or delayed collection, indicated by a bag remaining beside the collection-in-progress bin at S02-A-04.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** inadequate inspections or maintenance missed overflow at S02-A-01 and S02-A-05.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** existing bin numbers or capacity may not meet demand on busy park paths.<br>- **Verification:** review collection and inspection logs, capacity and usage data, peak waste surges, and missing or unclear sorting guidance. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, the problem may reduce visitor satisfaction and damage the scenic area's image, increase accumulation, vectors, odors, and public health risks, expose managers to repeated penalties affecting compliant operation, and normalize casual stockpiling, weakening waste sorting. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** remove the S02-A-04 bag; empty and replace liners in overflowing bins at S02-A-01 and S02-A-05; inspect all bins, repair or replace damaged or dirty containers, and sweep and disinfect disposal-point ground.<br>- **Long-term measures:** (1) increase bin numbers or capacity on busy paths; (2) adjust collection to visitor peaks; (3) strengthen inspections and overflow alerts using sensors or more frequent manual checks; (4) add sorting guidance and educational signs; (5) regularly train managers to implement regulations including the Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification. |
| Priority | **High.** Overflow and accumulation directly affect visitors and sanitation and breach multiple requirements for prompt removal and overflow prevention. Public health risks require immediate response and rectification to prevent escalation. |
